source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne Durham is the largest disclosed data center capacity in North Carolina at 40 MW, but 14 of the state's 19 mapped facilities publish no capacity, leaving the state's true compute inventory unknown.

The campus spans DUR1 and DUR2 with 420,000 square feet of technical space and represents 80 percent of North Carolina's disclosed IT capacity. That share is an artifact of disclosure, not proof of dominance. For AI, 40 MW is a published ceiling, not a confirmed workload; the operator gives no breakdown by tenant or accelerator type, so this facility cannot be counted as AI infrastructure on the data available.

The operator publishes no certifications, power infrastructure details, PUE, grid operator, or power purchase agreements, so the grid constraint on AI scaling cannot be assessed for this site. The suitability score of 69 reflects only published IT capacity and operator type, and it is missing an announced expansion signal. Durham is a known colocation footprint with an unknown power envelope and unknown AI utilization.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
